 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of M.V.Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) challenging the judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.1624/2007 on the file of Additional Senior NC: 2023:KHC:41233 Civil Judge and MACT-XIII at Madhugiri vide judgment dated 26.06.2012 in respect of liability.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the case are as under:
That on 28.11.2007 at 7.45 a.m. near Mudigowdanahalli on Tovinakere Nelahal Road,
the deceased Sunil Kumar was sitting in a tractor-trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TA-4421-4422 as a coolie to load and unload the jelly stones.

It is alleged that the driver of the tractor and trailer drove it in a rash and negligent manner as a M/S Icici Lombard General vs Eranna on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109613283/
2 result, of which Sunil Kumar fell down and died on the spot.
3. The claimants being the parents of the deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Act claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents.
4. The respondent No.1 was the owner of the tractor-trailer while respondent No.2 is the insurer.

The NC: 2023:KHC:41233 respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel and filed objection statement admitting that the deceased Sunil Kumar was working as a coolie under him and he further asserted that the vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.2 vide cover Note No.3008/3277825 and valid from 01.10.2007 to 30.09.2008 and the policy was in force at the time of the accident.
He also contended that the driver had a valid and effective driving licence.
5. The respondent No.2 has set up a defence that the driver did not possess valid and effective driving licence and there has been violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is further asserted that in fact, there was no insurance policy covering the offending vehicle and the policy which is relied is a fake policy and the respondent No.2 disputed his claim.

6. The tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence has allowed the petition in part by awarding a compensation of Rs.2,90,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition by NC: 2023:KHC:41233 fastening the liability on the respondents No.1 and 2 with primary liability on respondent No.2 - insurer.

Being aggrieved by this judgment and award,
the insurance company is before this court.
7. The learned counsel for the appellant - insurance company would contend that there is no dispute regarding quantum, but the liability itself is disputed as the claim is based on a fake policy.

He would contend that the cover note was said to have been covering the policy from 01.10.2007 to 30.09.2008 and the accident has occurred on 28.11.2007, but the policy itself is a fake policy and the policy under the said cover note was issued in respect of a different person and fraud has been played.
Hence, he would dispute the liability.

8. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent / claimant would contend that the cover note was issued by an authorized agent of the insurance company and if any fraud is played, it is for the respondent No.2 to take appropriate steps against its agent and since, the NC: 2023:KHC:41233 claimants being the third parties, they are liable to be reimbursed.
He would contend that the compensation awarded is also on the lower side and it needs to be enhanced.
He would contend that under Order 41 Rule 2 and under Order 41 Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, this court has ample power to enhance the compensation in order to avoid just compensation.
He placed reliance on a decision in 'THE ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. AKKAYAMMA & OTHERS', ILR 2009 KAR 24 in support of this claim.

sentences.text: 9. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, there is no serious dispute of the fact that the tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-06-TA-4421-4422 met with an accident on 28.11.2007.
It is also not in serious dispute that Sunil Kumar who was sitting on the tractor- trailer succumbed due to the injuries sustained in the said accident when he fell from the said tractor-trailer.

There is no M/S Icici Lombard General vs Eranna on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109613283/
3 serious dispute of the fact that the deceased was under the employment of respondent No.1 who was the NC: 2023:KHC:41233 owner.

sentences.text: The only contention of the insurance company is that the policy is a fake policy.
Hence, it is asserted that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

10. There is no serious dispute of the fact that the cover note No.ME 4795942 does not relate to the offending vehicle and it is pertaining to a different vehicle, but however, the Insurance Company has no where disputed that the cover note was issued by their authorized agent.
It is the specific assertion of the owner that he insured the vehicle through the authorized agent i.e., Sadakath.

11. RW1 is the officer of the insurance company and in his cross-examination, he admitted that in the year 2006-07, in Tumkur their office was not in existence and they used to issue policy through their agent.
He pleads ignorance as to how many agents were there for company, but admitted that Sadakath was the authorized agent of their company.
He also admitted that he was authorized to NC: 2023:KHC:41233 issue policy on behalf of the company.

He further admitted that they used to supply cover notes to the authorized agents for issuing the policy and in case of non issuance of the policy, the unused cover notes are required to be returned.
12.
Though in the instant case, there was a direction to produce the cover notes returned by Sadakath, the same was not produced by the Insurance Company.
13. Further RW1 In his further cross-examination admitted that Sadakath used to issue cover notes on behalf of the company.
Though he claims that on behalf of the company a number of fake policies have been issued, he admits that they have not taken any steps and it is asserted that they lodged a complaint with S.P.
There is no need for the insurance company to lodge a complaint with S.P. and they should have lodged a complaint with jurisdictional police in this regard.

It is also evident that regarding the issuance of fake policy by the agents, NC: 2023:KHC:41233 number of cases were registered and though they claimed that they have issued advisory to the clients, he admitted that it is not published in daily newspaper by giving vide publicity.

The further cross-examination of RW1 discloses that Sadakath was a contract employee and his services were provided by 'Team Lease'
Company.

When the said services of 'Team Lease' Company were utilized to secure the services of Sadakath, then the Insurance Company ought to have initiated necessary action against 'Team Lease' Company and they should have addressed letter to 'Team Lease' Company regarding fraud played by the employee whose services were provided to the appellant / Insurance Company.
But no such steps were taken and admittedly, Sakadath was the authorized agent of the Insurance Company.

Under such circumstances, the Insurance Company being the Principal is liable for the act of the agent as the sufferer is the clients and for the mischief committed by the agent of the Insurance Company, the clients cannot be held responsible and it is the duty of the Insurance Company to take appropriate - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41233 steps.

But the records discloses that no such steps were taken and no action was initiated against Sadakath and no request letter was issued to 'Team Lease' Company, which has provided the services of Sadakath to the Insurance Company for initiating the action.

M/S Icici Lombard General vs Eranna on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109613283/
4 14.

Looking to these facts and circumstances, the contention of the Insurance Company that since this is a fake policy, they are not liable cannot be accepted as the cover note was issued by the authorized agent which is at Ex.R6 /P14.
It is not the case of Insurance Company that the owner has created this policy.
Under these circumstances, the Insurance Company is liable for the act of the agent and they are at liberty to recover any damages from the concerned agent Sadakath.
15. The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that there is no serious dispute regarding quantum.

However, the learned counsel for the respondent / claimant would contend that the compensation awarded is on the lower side, but at the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41233 same time, the claimant has not filed any cross appeal under Order 41 Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but he invites the attention of the court to Order 41 Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

16. Under Order 41 Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the appellate court has power to pass any decree though the other side has not filed any appeal or objection statement and that right can be exercised.

Further, he has also invited the attention of the court to Order 41 Rule 2 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and argued that even by leave of the court; he can raise the objection set forth in memorandum of appeal.

In this context, he placed reliance on a decision reported in THE ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. AKKAYAMMA & OTHERS', ILR 2009 KAR 24 wherein the division bench decision of this court has observed as under:
"MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, -
SECTION 173(1)- INSURERE'S APPEAL-CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE,
1908-ORDER 41 RULE 33-Power of the Appellate Court-Exercise of - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41233 discretionary power-Expression "Which ought to have been passed" occurring in Order 41 Rule 33-HELD, The Appellate Court while exercising its discretionary power under Order 41 Rule 33 can pass any order to render complete justice between the parties.

entities.text: ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. AKKAYAMMA & OTHERS', ILR 2009 KAR 24
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On FACTS, HELD, The Motor Vehicle Claims Tribunal should have granted relief to the petitioner which ought in law to have been passed-The Tribunal has committed grave error while computing the loss of dependency by applying improper method and the same is apparently noticed.

In order to do complete justice to the parties, High Court can exercise its discretionary power under Order 41 Rule 33 CPC-Hence, compensation is enhanced to meet the ends of justice even though its is an appeal filed by the insurer."

17. The learned counsel for the appellant / Insurance Company has placed reliance on a decision of the Apex Court in 'SHIVAWWA AND ANR. VS. BRANCH MANAGER NATIONAL INDIA M/S Icici Lombard General vs Eranna on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109613283/
5 INSURANCE CO. LTD AND ANR.', AIR 2018 SC 1640, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed a under:
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41233 "(B) Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 1988), S.173 - Appeal-New Plea-Award of compensation passed by Tribunal-

entities.text: SHIVAWWA AND ANR. VS. BRANCH MANAGER NATIONAL INDIA M/S Icici Lombard General vs Eranna on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Claimant neither filed appeal for enhancement of compensation-Nor chose to file any cross-objection in first appeal filed by insurer before High court-Relief claimed by claimant only to set aside decision of High Court-Plea regarding quantum of compensation at instance of claimants-Cannot be allowed to be raised for first time in appeal."

18. Though under Order 41 Rule 33 of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, this court has got ample power, but in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court when the claimant has neither filed an appeal for enhancement nor chose to file cross objection in the appeal filed by the insurer,
question of entertaining the claim of enhancement of compensation does not arise at all.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court as referred to supra, the decision reported in THE ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. AKKAYAMMA & OTHERS', ILR 2009 KAR 24 cannot be applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case in hand.

entities.text: ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. AKKAYAMMA & OTHERS', ILR 2009 KAR 24
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, question of enhancing the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:41233 compensation does not arise at all.
In view of the same, the appeal needs to be dismissed and the respondent No.2 i.e., the appellant herein is required to pay the entire compensation as awarded by the tribunal.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the appellants is dismissed.

Sd/-

The reasoning discloses that, though it is a fake policy but the agent-Sadakath has played M/S Icici Lombard General vs Eranna on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109613283/
6 fraud on the owner of the offending vehicle, and thereby liability is fastened on the insurance company on the ground that the act of agent is binding on the principal.
